messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PagerDuty PD12345 fired for tenant solis_tenant_id on dedicated pool rsv-4-west (cluster: solis-prod-reserved). Symptoms: sustained 5xx spike, p95 latency > 6s. Alerts: reserved-pool-latency, tenant-503-rate. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-latency

pagerduty-bot: Paging @Alyssa (primary oncall) — please acknowledge PD12345.

Alyssa (oncall): ack — I'm on it. What's the user impact right now? @Liam can you confirm if SolisHealth is seeing customer-facing errors? :eyes: 

Liam (cs): got a DM from SolisHealth SRE. They report ~20% 503 on their POST /search endpoint over the last 10m, intermittent timeouts. Not yet public-facing but they flagged it as impacting internal dashboards.

Maya (eng-runtime): grabbing metrics — p95 token latency went from 2.3s to 8.1s in the last 15m. 503 rate for solis_tenant_id ~18%. Observed KV cache evictions/sec spike: 480 -> 3200, and batch sizes dropped (avg batch size 6 -> 2). Suspect KV cache thrash + reserved pool underprovisioning.

Jamal (sre): can we divert some traffic to shared pools or bump reserved capacity? I'll attempt routing fallback then scale the pool.

Alyssa (oncall): prefer safe mitigations first — increase pool by +2 nodes, enable fallback to shared-burst for tenant, and reduce batch size to lower memory pressure. Avoid full redeploy unless needed.

Maya (eng-runtime): executing mitigation commands now:
```bash
redwoodctl pools scale --pool-id rsv-4-west --add-nodes 2 --reason "sustained latency PD12345"
redwoodctl routing set --tenant solis_tenant_id --fallback shared-burst --enable
# reduce default batch size for affected model
redwoodctl config set --model default --batch-size 16
```

Ops-Bot: Command accepted: scaling rsv-4-west +2 nodes (desired=10). Estimated time to active: ~90s.

Ops-Bot: Routing change queued. Applying fallback for tenant solis_tenant_id -> shared-burst.

Ops-Bot: Routing update applied: traffic split for solis_tenant_id = 80% reserved / 20% shared-burst.

Maya (eng-runtime): immediate signal: 503 rate dropping 18% -> 6% within 2m, p95 latency down to ~1.9s. KV eviction rate decreasing. Looks like fallback + scale bought us headroom. :thumbsup: 

Jamal (sre): while scaling, noticed scheduler backlog on node-71 leading to OOM kills and redwood-driver restarts. Restarting service on node-71 now.

Jamal (sre): ran:
```bash
ssh ops@node-71
sudo systemctl restart redwood-driver
# cleared oom logs, verifying container restarts
journalctl -u redwood-driver -n 50 --no-pager | tail -n 20
```
Node-71 recovered, no further OOMs after restart.

Liam (cs): SolisHealth SRE confirms partial recovery, errors reduced significantly. They still see occasional 503s but much better than earlier.

Alyssa (oncall): good. I've acknowledged PD12345. Setting incident state -> monitoring. I'll keep watch for 1 hour, then handoff to Jamal for overnight. Please keep alerts tightened.

Ops-Bot: PD incident PD12345 updated: status=acknowledged, priority lowered P1 -> P2 (per runbook threshold).

Maya (eng-runtime): created initial incident notes and a draft postmortem: /docs/incidents/PD12345.md. Initial hypothesis: KV cache thrash + scheduler OOM on one node caused reserved pool capacity pressure. Early recommendations: tune autoscaler to be less reactive to transient bursts, increase cache allocation for solis_tenant_id, and improve scheduler resource isolation.

Alyssa (oncall): tagging for escalation path — @pagerduty-bot please escalate to infra-team if 503_rate > 10% for more than 5m. For now, handing off active watch to Jamal.

Jamal (sre): taking handoff. I'll adjust alert thresholds: 503_rate threshold -> 5% and p95 latency -> 3s for escalations. I'll escalate to infra if thresholds breach.

Alyssa (oncall): handoff complete. Handoff note: mitigations applied (scale + routing fallback + node restart), customer impact reduced, monitoring in place. Oncall -> Jamal.

Ops-Bot: Incident PD12345 marked as monitoring, owner=Jamal (sre).

Alyssa (oncall): thanks everyone. Follow-up action items in the postmortem draft: autoscaler tuning, cache sizing per-tenant, and adding a runbook step to prefer routing fallback before scale for noisy tenants. Will sync during morning triage. :eyes: :thumbsup:

Jamal (sre): will follow up overnight if anything comes up.

incident-bot: (system) thread closed to further automated paging for PD12345 — status=monitoring.
